title: query_matches team filter is case-sensitive — capitalized team names return zero matches
evidence: server.py:201 `if team and team not in home_team and team not in away_team` compares the RAW arg against normalize_team_name(...) output which is lowercased (server.py:106). Repro: team='Flamengo' -> 'Flamengo' in 'flamengo' == False, so every row is skipped and 'Found 0 matches' is returned. The spec's own examples use capitalized names ('all Flamengo vs Fluminense matches', TASK.md:164). By contrast query_competition:456 and analyze_statistics:563 DO call team.lower(), confirming this is an inconsistency, not pre-normalization.
suggestion: Lowercase/normalize the `team` (and `opponent`) argument before the membership test, as query_competition already does.

title: query_team_stats team filter has the same case-sensitivity defect
evidence: server.py:292-293 `is_home = team in home_team` / `is_away = team in away_team` compare the raw arg against lowercased normalized names (server.py:288-289). A capitalized team (e.g. 'Corinthians', as in test_server.py:141) yields matches=0 and an all-zero W/L/D/goals record. Tests pass only because they assert the header string, not the counts (test_server.py:123-144 check for 'Team Statistics'/'Wins:' substrings, never the numeric values).
suggestion: Normalize/lowercase the `team` argument once at the top of query_team_stats before comparison.

title: No ranked season standings/league table — only single-team points are computed
evidence: server.py:461-511 query_competition computes points/W-L-D for a SINGLE team only when `team` is supplied (points at server.py:508); with no team it just lists raw matches (server.py:512-517). grep for standing/position/rank/table finds no code that ranks all teams by points into a positional table. R9 (how_to_verify: 'Standings (points/positions) computed from matches') asks for a season standings table with positions across all teams. Points-from-matches exists for one team, but there is no multi-team ranked standings.
suggestion: Add a standings path in query_competition when no team is given: aggregate points/GD for every team over the season and emit a ranked table with positions.

title: query_matches competition filter only matches internal dataset keys, not the documented competition names
evidence: server.py:192 `if competition and file_key != competition` requires an exact match against internal keys ('brasileirao','copa_brasil','libertadores'). A user/LLM passing 'Copa do Brasil' or 'Libertadores' (capitalized, as the docstring at server.py:181 and spec suggest) matches no file_key, so all datasets are skipped -> 0 matches. query_competition:430-437 has a name->key map; query_matches does not reuse it.
suggestion: Reuse the competition name->key mapping from query_competition inside query_matches so display names resolve to dataset keys.

title: Tests assert only response header substrings, not result counts — masking the R3/R6 case bugs
evidence: Every query test asserts `len(results) == 1` (the TextContent list wrapper, always length 1) plus header substrings like 'Found'/'Team Statistics' (test_server.py:87-113,123-144). None assert the actual match/win counts, so the case-sensitivity defects that make query_matches/query_team_stats return zero results still pass. defect_rate=1.0 in scores.json reflects passing-but-shallow tests.
suggestion: Assert on concrete numeric outcomes (e.g. Flamengo 2023 match count > 0, non-zero wins) so behavioral regressions are caught.
